name: Joshua Rotenberg
role: Business Systems Analyst, Sales AI & Automation
body: This role is close to a description of what I already do at Solenzo, the company I founded: sit between a revenue team's real friction points and the automated system that fixes them, then build it myself instead of handing off a spec. I've shipped 20+ production automation workflows there, covering lead capture, qualification, appointment booking, and retention, and I'd like to bring that same builder posture to your GTM team.

Three things map directly to what you've described. First, I regularly translate a non-technical stakeholder's loosely defined idea into a working AI agent, writing the prompts and instructions myself and iterating until the output holds up. Second, I've built rubric-based grading criteria to evaluate AI agent output quality and do the underlying data labeling personally, the same discipline behind guarding cost, performance, and trust in a shipped workflow. Third, when a no-code platform's point-and-click config runs out of road, I write the Python or JavaScript code step that gets it the rest of the way, and I pull the SQL behind my own Power BI and BigQuery/GA4 reporting rather than waiting on someone else to hand me a dashboard.

I've touched Salesforce from the strategy side too: at Wix, I advised on A/B testing for a Salesforce workflow-automation effort, defining test structure and success criteria for the team building it. I haven't built inside Salesforce as an admin myself, though, and tools like Clay or Snowflake aren't yet in my stack, I'd rather say that directly than paper over it. What I bring instead is a demonstrated ability to pick up a new system fast and ship with it, at a scale where I was the only engineer, PM, and support desk for every workflow I built. I'd welcome the chance to talk through how that translates to your team.
